findings.message:
Credential pattern is declared twice and can silently diverge

`AuthScheme::pattern()` is the runtime source of truth. The snapshot derives `scheme_pattern` from it (`crates/credential/src/snapshot.rs:152`), and the derive macro fills `CredentialDescription::pattern` from `<Scheme as AuthScheme>::pattern()` (`crates/credential/macros/src/credential.rs:123`). The hand-written `Credential::description()` impls instead set `pattern` to a literal. The field is a required, independent value (`crates/credential/src/description.rs:63`, enforced at `:149`). Nothing compares the two. Changing a credential's `type Scheme` without editing `description()` leaves the UI/tooling pattern stale, with no compile-time or runtime error.

Fix: in the hand-written impls, set `pattern` from `<Self::Scheme as nebula_core::AuthScheme>::pattern()`, the same expression the macro emits. Or remove the field from the authoring path and derive it where the description is built.

Lazy rotation in `get()` returns a stale version, and a failed rewrite fails the read

- On a successful rewrite the store bumps the version (`crates/credential/src/store_memory.rs:91`), but `get()` returns the pre-write `credential` with the old version (`:152`). The resolver's refresh path CAS-writes with `stored.version`, so the first refresh after rotation hits `VersionConflict`, logs a warning, and retries. The data stays correct, but each rotated record costs an extra write and a spurious warning.
- Only `VersionConflict` from the rewrite is tolerated (`:147`). Any other backend error is returned (`:148`), so a read whose decryption succeeded fails when the write fails. The surrounding comment treats rotation as opportunistic ("rotation will happen on next read").

Fix: on success, copy the stored version into the returned record (for example `Ok(stored) => credential.version = stored.version`). Decide explicitly whether a non-conflict rewrite failure should be logged while the plaintext is returned.

The empty `key_id` contract is documented two different ways

The `EncryptedData::key_id` doc says the layer "rejects empty key IDs at runtime — a migration must re-encrypt all records before upgrading." But `EncryptionLayer::new()` registers `""` as a live alias for its key (`:69`), so pre-rotation envelopes decrypt and are rewritten under `"default"`. `with_keys()` registers no alias (`:92`), so the same records fail with "encryption key '' not found — cannot decrypt". The doc matches neither constructor. A deployment that moves from `new()` to `with_keys()` cannot read pre-rotation records.

Fix: pick one rule. Either remove the `""` alias so both constructors reject empty IDs, or make legacy support an explicit option that both honor. Update the `key_id` doc to match.

`with_keys()` silently drops duplicate key IDs

`collect()` into a `HashMap` keeps the last entry for a repeated ID without error. A copy-paste duplicate when adding a rotation key silently discards the earlier key. Records encrypted under it then fail AEAD verification with a generic backend error that never mentions the duplicate. The constructor already asserts the current-key invariant (`:93-96`), so a duplicate check belongs next to it.

Fix: assert, or return an error, when an ID appears twice.

Webhook rate-limit doc states the wrong path cap

The doc on `WebhookRateLimiter::new` now reads "At most 1 000 distinct paths are tracked." `DEFAULT_MAX_PATHS` is `10_000` (`:23`) and `new()` uses it (`:71`), so the limiter tracks ten times more paths than the doc says. Commit `d5ba86d` replaced a broken intra-doc link to the private constant with this literal.

Fix: write "10 000" to match the constant, or write "`DEFAULT_MAX_PATHS` (10 000)" in code formatting.

`encrypt` and `encrypt_with_aad` can stamp an empty `key_id`, and the sealing logic is repeated three times

`encrypt_with_key_id` (`crates/credential/src/crypto.rs:366`, empty-ID guard at `:372`) is the only one that enforces the key-ID rule, and the production write path uses it (`crates/credential/src/layer/encryption.rs:187`). The other two build `EncryptedData::new("", …)`. Their callers are tests only, so the gap is latent. The three near-identical bodies also mean any sealing fix must land in three places.

Fix: extract one private seal helper that requires a non-empty key ID. Then remove `encrypt` and `encrypt_with_aad`, or route them through it.

`From<OAuth2Token> for SecretToken` drops the token's expiry

`AuthScheme::expires_at()` is the lifetime contract the framework uses to schedule auto-refresh (`crates/core/src/auth.rs:59-63`). The conversion builds `SecretToken::new(access_token)` alone. `SecretToken` has no expiry field, so the result never expires. The conversion is infallible, and its doc table says only "Always (extracts access_token)". No production caller in the repo uses it today, so the impact falls on future callers.

Fix: carry the lifetime in `SecretToken` (an optional expiry returned from `expires_at()`), or drop the infallible conversion so callers handle the lifetime explicitly.

The snapshot stores the scheme pattern as a Debug string

`CredentialSnapshot` stores `format!("{:?}", S::pattern())` and exposes it as `scheme_pattern() -> &str`. `AuthPattern` is a `Copy + Eq + Hash` enum with no `Display` or `as_str`, so the public string is whatever derived `Debug` prints. Renaming a variant silently changes the public value, and callers must string-match literals with no compiler help. The `SchemeMismatch` error is built from the same strings.

Fix: store `AuthPattern` in the snapshot, expose it through a typed accessor, and format names only at the display boundary.

The KeyPair round-trip test no longer covers passphrase or algorithm

`key_pair_serde_roundtrip` builds the pair with `KeyPair::new(...)` only, so `passphrase` and `algorithm` stay `None`, and the test asserts only the two key fields. The deleted `ssh_auth_keypair_serde_roundtrip` (old line 147) set a passphrase and asserted `json.contains("my-passphrase")`. As written, a serializer that drops or redacts the passphrase, or skips `algorithm`, would still pass.

Fix: add a case built with `.with_passphrase(SecretString::new("my-passphrase")).with_algorithm("ed25519")`. Assert the passphrase appears in the JSON and that `algorithm()` round-trips.
